types.name: ArgPortInput
types.description:
A Port is a single input or output of an action, identified by its `key` and typed by its `kind`.

    STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE ports carry an `identifier` of the form `@package/key`
    (e.g. `@mikro/image`); ports with the same identifier are compatible. LIST and DICT ports have one
    child (the item type), UNION ports two or more (the variants), MODEL ports one per field. ENUM ports
    declare `choices`. See docs/design/ports.md for the full table.

inputFields.name: children
inputFields.description: The child ports (used for list, dict, union and model ports).

inputFields.name: choices
inputFields.description: The values the port accepts (required for ENUM; optional for INT, FLOAT, STRING). Rendered by CHOICE widgets.

inputFields.name: default
inputFields.description: The default value for the port; must fit the port's kind.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: The description of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI when the user hovers over the port

inputFields.name: dimension
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the pint dimensionality string, e.g. "[mass] * [length] ** 2 / [time] ** 3 / [current]". This is the wiring-compatibility key between quantity ports.

inputFields.name: effects
inputFields.description: The effects of the port

inputFields.name: identifier
inputFields.description: The identifier of a structure port. This is used to uniquely identify a specific type of structure.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The key of the port: unique among its siblings, free of '..', not 'value'. LIST/DICT item ports are conventionally keyed '...'.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: The kind of the port. This is the type of the port. Can be either int, string, structure, list, bool, dict, float, date, union or model

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: The label of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI

inputFields.name: nullable
inputFields.description: Whether the port is nullable or not. If the port is nullable, it can be set to null. If the port is not nullable, it cannot be set to null

inputFields.name: proposedUnits
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: units offered as a dropdown in the UI, e.g. ["pF", "nF", "uF"]. Proposals only — any unit of the same dimension remains valid input.

inputFields.name: referenceUnit
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the canonical/reference unit of the physical quantity, e.g. "volt" or "farad". It is the default selection and the key used to resolve the concrete quantity type; other units of the same dimension are still allowed.

inputFields.name: requires
inputFields.description: The descriptors for the port. Descriptors are key-value pairs that can be used to add additional metadata to a port. When using rekuest's action search, you can filter actions based on their port descriptors

inputFields.name: validators
inputFields.description: The validators for the port

inputFields.name: widget
inputFields.description: The assign widget to use for this port, discriminated by `kind`.

types.description: An assign widget: the UI element used to assign a value to a port, as a discriminated union over `kind`. Only the fields of the chosen kind may be set; see the `*AssignWidgetInput` members.

inputFields.name: asParagraph
inputFields.description: (STRING) Render as a multi-line paragraph.

inputFields.name: component
inputFields.description: (CUSTOM) The catalog component to render. The port value is in scope as the reserved root `value`.

inputFields.name: dependencies
inputFields.description: (SEARCH, CUSTOM, STATE_CHOICE) The other ports (port paths, `..` traverses children) whose values the query may reference.

inputFields.name: dependency
inputFields.description: (STATE_CHOICE) The agent dependency (by key) whose state provides the choices; omitted: the implementing agent's own state.

inputFields.name: fallback
inputFields.description: (CUSTOM) Widget to render when the UI has no such component in its catalog.

inputFields.name: filters
inputFields.description: (SEARCH) Filter ports whose values are passed to the query as variables named by their keys.

inputFields.name: followValue
inputFields.description: (SLIDER, CHOICE, STRING, SEARCH, CUSTOM, STATE_CHOICE, PROXY) Port path of another port whose value this widget follows and mirrors.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Which kind of assign widget this is; decides which other fields are read.

inputFields.name: max
inputFields.description: (SLIDER) The maximum value.

inputFields.name: min
inputFields.description: (SLIDER) The minimum value.

inputFields.name: placeholder
inputFields.description: (CHOICE, STRING, SEARCH) The placeholder text shown before a choice is made. The choices themselves are the port's `choices`.

inputFields.name: props
inputFields.description: (CUSTOM) Props of the component. value_paths may only reference `value` and `dependencies`; agent calls are not allowed.

inputFields.name: query
inputFields.description: (SEARCH) The GraphQL query the ward executes to populate the choices. Must be a single `query` operation declaring `$search: String` and `$values: [ID!]`, plus one variable per filter port key.

inputFields.name: stateAccessors
inputFields.description: (STATE_CHOICE) How to read label/description/logo/value out of each state entry; each accessor is a static pointer or a pure call.

inputFields.name: stateCall
inputFields.description: (STATE_CHOICE) Pure UtilCall returning that pointer dynamically; may reference `state`, `value` and `dependencies`. Mutually exclusive with `state_path`.

inputFields.name: statePath
inputFields.description: (STATE_CHOICE) Static JSON pointer into the state value that provides the choices. Mutually exclusive with `state_call`.

inputFields.name: step
inputFields.description: (SLIDER) The step between selectable values; must be positive.

inputFields.name: targetAction
inputFields.description: (PROXY) The action to target: an action-dependency key of `target_dependency` when that is set.

inputFields.name: targetDependency
inputFields.description: (PROXY) The agent dependency (by key) that provides the targeted action; omitted: the implementing agent itself.

inputFields.name: targetPort
inputFields.description: (PROXY) The port key on the targeted action.

types.name: EffectInput
types.description:
An effect is a way to modify a port based on a condition. For example,
    you could have an effect that hides the port if another port meets a condition,
    e.g. when the user selects a certain option in a dropdown, another port is hidden.

    The condition is a pure blok UtilCall (`call`) evaluated client-side against the
    catalog; it must return a boolean deciding whether the effect applies. `dependencies`
    is the authoritative list of other ports the call may reference (plus `value` for the
    port's own value).

inputFields.name: call
inputFields.description: The pure blok UtilCall, evaluated client-side against the catalog, that decides whether the effect applies. It must return a boolean. Argument value_paths may only reference names listed in `dependencies`, plus `value` for the port's own value.

inputFields.name: dependencies
inputFields.description: The form-field subscription list of the effect: the keys of the other ports whose values the call may reference. This list is authoritative: a value_path in the call may only reference these names (plus `value` for the port's own value). Use the .. syntax to traverse the tree of ports, e.g. 'foo..bar' for the child 'bar' of port 'foo'.

inputFields.name: fade
inputFields.description: Whether to fade out the port when the effect is applied (if it is a hide effect)

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: The kind of the effect. Can be either message, hide or custom

inputFields.name: message
inputFields.description: The message to display when the effect is applied (if it is a message effect)

inputFields.name: source
inputFields.description: The authoring expression the call was compiled from (informational; never parsed or validated by the server).

enumValues.name: MODEL
enumValues.description: An object with named fields; at least one child per field, `identifier` optional.

enumValues.name: QUANTITY

enumValues.name: UNION

types.name: ReturnPortInput
types.description:
A Port is a single input or output of an action, identified by its `key` and typed by its `kind`.

    STRUCTURE, MEMORY_STRUCTURE and INTERFACE ports carry an `identifier` of the form `@package/key`
    (e.g. `@mikro/image`); ports with the same identifier are compatible. LIST and DICT ports have one
    child (the item type), UNION ports two or more (the variants), MODEL ports one per field. ENUM ports
    declare `choices`. See docs/design/ports.md for the full table.

inputFields.name: children
inputFields.description: The child ports (used for list, dict, union and model ports).

inputFields.name: choices
inputFields.description: The values the port accepts (required for ENUM; optional for INT, FLOAT, STRING). Rendered by CHOICE widgets.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: The description of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI when the user hovers over the port

inputFields.name: dimension
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the pint dimensionality string, e.g. "[mass] * [length] ** 2 / [time] ** 3 / [current]". This is the wiring-compatibility key between quantity ports.

inputFields.name: effects
inputFields.description: The effects of the port

inputFields.name: identifier
inputFields.description: The identifier of a structure port. This is used to uniquely identify a specific type of structure.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description: The key of the port: unique among its siblings, free of '..', not 'value'. LIST/DICT item ports are conventionally keyed '...'.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: The kind of the port. This is the type of the port. Can be either int, string, structure, list, bool, dict, float, date, union or model

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: The label of the port. This is the text that is displayed in the UI

inputFields.name: nullable
inputFields.description: Whether the port is nullable or not. If the port is nullable, it can be set to null. If the port is not nullable, it cannot be set to null

inputFields.name: proposedUnits
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: units offered as a dropdown in the UI, e.g. ["pF", "nF", "uF"]. Proposals only — any unit of the same dimension remains valid input.

inputFields.name: provides
inputFields.description: The provisions for the port. Provisions are key-value pairs that can be used to add additional metadata to a port. When using rekuest's action search, you can filter actions based on their port provisions

inputFields.name: referenceUnit
inputFields.description: For QUANTITY ports: the canonical/reference unit of the physical quantity, e.g. "volt" or "farad". It is the default selection and the key used to resolve the concrete quantity type; other units of the same dimension are still allowed.

inputFields.name: widget
inputFields.description: The return widget to use for this port, discriminated by `kind`.

types.name: ReturnWidgetInput
types.description: A return widget: the UI element used to display a port's value, as a discriminated union over `kind`. Only the fields of the chosen kind may be set; see the `*ReturnWidgetInput` members.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Which kind of return widget this is; decides which other fields are read.

inputFields.name: props
inputFields.description: (CUSTOM) Props of the component; value_paths may only reference `value`, agent calls are not allowed.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.
